item.title: Applications — claimed vs shipped
item.description:
One shelf. [[notice|Notice]] · [[citations|Citations]] · [[reference/forms]] · [[topics/manufacturing/directory]]

What actually leaves a plant

  • Composites / elastomers — [[topics/manufacturing/pacific-urethanes]] + PureGRAPH mining PU. Fire class unpublished.
  • Coatings / inks — [[topics/industry/thermal-xr|THERMAL-XR]]. [[topics/industry/sparc-hydrograph-coatings|Sparc × HydroGraph]] ISO 9227 / 12944 (Preliminary). Vor-ink. [[topics/industry/genable-pavement|Genable Pavement]] (lays named; durability Preliminary).
  • Energy-storage additives — [[topics/manufacturing/conovate|eCOphite]]. GMG 10C Preliminary.
  • Films / heaters / fluids — [[topics/industry/justheat|JustHeat]] 62 W / 48 V. [[topics/industry/haydale-settf|SETTF]] (Preliminary). Charmgraphene / 2D Carbon heater film.
  • Media / PPE / textiles — [[topics/industry/zenguard|ZenGUARD]] (MERV 9 company 52.2). [[topics/industry/directa-gplus|Directa G+]].
  • Lab GO membranes — Nair 2012 / Abraham 2017.
  • Sensors / RF — [[posts/holey-graphene-molecular-stencil]]
  • Tools — [[topics/manufacturing/cvd-equipment]]

Did not ship as sold

Replace silicon. ITO tomorrow. “The graphene battery” as one object. [[logs/theories]]

item.title: Common mix-ups
item.description:
Language

  • Graphite = graphene. No. [[reference/forms]]
  • GO = graphene. No.
  • A nanoplatelet tonne = a monolayer wafer. No.
  • Wallace or Boehm “discovered graphene” in the 2004 sense. Too coarse. [[timeline/1947]] · [[timeline/1962]] · [[timeline/2004]]

Physics-as-product

  • Ideal monolayer tensile strength applies to a bulk composite at face value. No. [[reference/properties]]
  • f_T of 100–155 GHz means graphene CPUs this decade. No. [[timeline/2011]]
  • Flagship €1bn was a 2013 bank deposit. No. [[timeline/2013]]

Health / rumor

  • Nanosafety paper ⇒ covert deployment in vaccines or air. Non sequitur. [[reference/safety]] · [[logs/conspiracies]]
  • GO on a cryo-EM grid ⇒ GO in a licensed shot. No. [[topics/fringe/2026-09-16-go-vaccine-5g-claims]]

Recurrence

Old papers resurfacing as “breaking” (UCLA stencil 2015 paper in a 2026 CMS page). [[recurrence/log]] · [[posts/holey-graphene-molecular-stencil]]

item.title: Forms of the graphene family
item.description:
Evidence: Well-supported as materials taxonomy. A bag labeled “graphene” is not thereby a 2004 Manchester flake.

If one page on this site should survive a server migration, it is this one. Most arguments about graphene are arguments about which solid.

Pristine sheets

  • Monolayer graphene — one honeycomb plane of sp² carbon. The object of [[timeline/2004]] and [[timeline/1947]].
  • Bilayer / few-layer (FLG) — two to roughly ten planes. Electronic structure changes with layer number and stacking. Magic-angle twisted bilayer is a stacking-and-angle story ([[timeline/2018]]), not a powder grade.
  • Graphite — many planes, 3D crystal. Parent material ([[timeline/pre-chemistry]]).

Chemically derived

  • Graphite oxide — oxidized, lamellar graphite (Brodie lineage, [[timeline/before-1900]]).
  • Graphene oxide (GO) — exfoliated oxidized sheets; hydrophilic; insulating compared with graphene; processable in water.
  • Reduced graphene oxide (rGO) — GO with oxygen stripped back. More conductive than GO, more defective than cleaved or good CVD graphene.

Industrial grades (names vary by vendor)

  • Nanoplatelets / GNP — stacks that may be tens of layers. Often what “tonnes of graphene” means.
  • CVD film — grown on metal (Cu landmark: [[timeline/2009]]), transferred. Grain boundaries and wrinkles are part of the object.
  • Epitaxial graphene on SiC — carbon left after Si leaves the surface. IBM 100 GHz FETs used this family ([[timeline/2010]]).
  • Graphene quantum dots (GQDs) — very small pieces with confined electronics and photoluminescence claims; quality varies wildly.
  • Foams, aerogels, fibres, yarns — assembled architectures (e.g. wet-spun GO fibres in [[weekly/2026-W38]]).
  • Holey / perforated graphene — engineered holes; mask or membrane, not a synonym for GO ([[posts/holey-graphene-molecular-stencil]]).

Naming collisions

  • Graphene monoxide / eCOphite — company chemistry ([[topics/finance/2026-09-15-conovate-doe-award]]), not GO.
  • “Graphene battery” in a headline may mean a conductive additive, a coating, an anode experiment, or wishful copy.

See [[reference/misconceptions]] and [[guides/glossary]].

item.title: How graphene-family materials are made
item.description:
Evidence: Well-supported as a process map. Capacity announcements are not grades.

Mechanical cleavage

Scotch-tape / micromechanical exfoliation from graphite. Best flakes for physics. Terrible area. [[timeline/2004]]

Epitaxy on SiC

Heat SiC; Si leaves; carbon rearranges. Wafer-ish, substrate-bound, expensive. IBM 100 GHz FETs ([[timeline/2010]]).

CVD on metal

Grow on Cu (landmark [[timeline/2009]]) or Ni; transfer off. Path to large optical films ([[timeline/2010]] Bae). Defects: grains, wrinkles, transfer residue, cracks.

Oxide route

Oxidize graphite (Brodie / Staudenmaier / Hummers), exfoliate to GO, optionally reduce to rGO. Scalable, dirty, hydrophilic. [[timeline/before-1900]] · [[timeline/1962]]

item.title: ISO and IEC graphene wording
item.description:
Evidence: Well-supported that these documents exist and carry these years. Clause text lives in the paid file.

Parent: [[reference/index]] · [[guides/glossary]] · [[timeline/2017]]

Vocabulary

  • ISO/TS 80004-13:2017 — Nanotechnologies — Vocabulary — Part 13: Graphene and related two-dimensional materials. First edition.
  • ISO/TS 80004-13:2024 — Second edition (Sep 2024). Cancels 2017. Adds graphene-related 2D material (GR2M) among other revisions. Joint ISO/IEC circulation in the draft trail.
  • Related core vocab still cited by those parts: ISO/TS 80004-1 (core terms), 80004-2 (nano-objects), 80004-6 (nano-object characterization).

Structural characterization of powders and dispersions

  • ISO/TS 21356-1:2021 (first edition, March 2021). Sequence of methods after isolating flakes: layer number / thickness, lateral size, disorder, layer alignment, specific surface area. Covers graphene, bilayer, nanoplatelets from powder or liquid. Raman, SEM, AFM, TEM, BET in the usual toolkit. CEN adopted as CEN ISO/TS 21356-1:2022.

How this site maps the words

Site word We mean Do not hear
Graphene Honeycomb sheet; say monolayer if we mean one layer Any black powder
FLG A few layers, when the paper counts them GO paper
GNP / nanoplatelet Thicker stack sold as graphene 2004 Manchester flake
GO Oxidized sheets from graphite oxide Vaccine antigen
rGO GO with oxygen pulled back Defect-free CVD
CVD film Grown then often transferred 4,000 t powder
GR2M ISO 2024 umbrella for graphene-related 2D materials A new allotrope

What a standard is not

Not a bag certificate. Not a health clearance. Not proof a vendor is “ISO graphene certified” because the letters appear on a slide.

item.title: Properties — ideal sheet vs real sample
item.description:
Evidence: Well-supported that the ideal monolayer has extraordinary calculated and measured properties. Transferring those numbers onto a painted wall or a 1 Ah cell is a separate claim.

Electronic

  • Linear bands near the Dirac points ([[timeline/1947]], [[timeline/2005]]).
  • High mobility on good samples, especially encapsulated on hBN ([[timeline/2010]], [[timeline/2012]]).
  • No native band gap in monolayer graphene. That is why digital-logic replacement of silicon stalled as an engineering ideal ([[timeline/2011]], [[logs/theories]]).
  • Bilayers, nanoribbons, and certain stacks can open gaps — different objects.

Mechanical

  • Intrinsic strength and stiffness of a pristine monolayer are among the highest measured for a 2D crystal (Lee / Hone Science 2008 nanoindentation is the usual citation). A polymer with 0.1 wt% platelets does not inherit that tensile strength.

Thermal / optical

  • High in-plane thermal conductivity on clean samples; grain boundaries, wrinkles, and matrix interfaces dominate real heat-spreader products.
  • Visible transparency of a monolayer is ~97.7% (Nair et al., Science 2008 is the usual optical landmark). That number made transparent-electrode pitches easy to write ([[timeline/2010]] Bae film).

Chemical

  • Basal plane is relatively inert; edges and defects are where chemistry happens. That is why a stencil on gold is about holes and edges ([[posts/holey-graphene-molecular-stencil]]) and why GO is a different substance.

Rule for readers

Ask: which form ([[reference/forms]]), how measured, in what matrix, at what loading. If a press release quotes the ideal monolayer next to a bulk product, that is rhetoric.

item.title: Related 2D materials
item.description:
Evidence: Well-supported that these crystals are studied in the same labs and programmes (Flagship mandate included “related layered materials”: [[timeline/2013]]).

  • hBN — insulating honeycomb; the preferred encapsulant / substrate for clean graphene transport ([[timeline/2010]] Dean).
  • TMDCs (MoS₂, WS₂, …) — many have a band gap; different electronics than graphene.
  • Phosphorene, silicene, MXenes, etc. — separate literatures. Mention when a source actually uses them; do not absorb them into “graphene news.”

Twisted stacks and heterostructures are how these combine ([[timeline/2012]], [[timeline/2018]]).

item.title: Safety, exposure, toxicology
item.description:
Evidence: Mixed. Field hygiene data can be well-supported. Many cell-culture papers are preliminary. Nothing here is medical advice.

Full effects table (humans, animals, workplace numbers): [[topics/health/effects]].

What is actually measured at work

NIOSH sampled workers at US graphene producers/users. Against a conservative 10 µg/m³ occupational band (not an OSHA PEL), many samples exceeded it when dry powder was handled. Prefer masterbatch or liquid in that literature. [[topics/policy/2026-09-16-niosh-graphene-exposure]] · [[weekly/2026-W38]]

No disease cluster is attached to those notes on this site. Absence of a reported cluster is not proof of lifelong safety.

item.title: Standards and quality
item.description:
Evidence: Well-supported that ISO/IEC vocabulary and related technical specs exist. They do not certify a random SKU.

Why this page exists

After ~2014, “graphene” on an invoice could mean almost any of [[reference/forms]]. Purchasing fights are about layer number, lateral size, oxygen content, metal residue, and surface area — not Dirac cones.

Documented landmarks

  • ISO/TS 80004-13:2017 — vocabulary for graphene and related two-dimensional carbons ([[timeline/2017]]). Its value is admitting multiple materials.
  • National measurement labs (NPL and peers) publish characterization good-practice notes (Raman, XPS, AFM, TGA). Use the lab document, not a tweet summarizing it.
  • Flagship and national projects spent years on protocols; protocols ≠ enforcement.

Practical reader checklist

  1. Which form?
  2. Layer distribution, not a single magic number.
  3. Oxygen / defect metric (XPS, Raman D/G).
  4. Metals and residual solvent.
  5. Dry powder vs masterbatch ([[topics/policy/2026-09-16-niosh-graphene-exposure]]).

If a vendor will not answer those, the archive can still list the press release — under Preliminary or Unverified.
